meta.title: Sindh JEST Guess Paper - Subject-wise Easy, Normal and Hard MCQs
meta.description: Subject-wise Sindh Junior Elementary School Teacher preparation bank with 30 Easy, 30 Normal and 30 Hard MCQs for each JEST area.
meta.keywords: Sindh JEST, Junior Elementary School Teacher, STS, English, Mathematics, General Science, Computer, General Knowledge, IQ, Pedagogy, Assessment, Education, Social Studies, Urdu, Sindhi

questions.q: Choose the correct synonym for the word 'big'.
questions.ex: 'Large' is a synonym of 'big'.

questions.q: Select the correct plural form of 'child'.
questions.ex: Irregular plural of 'child' is 'children'.

questions.q: Which word is an adjective in the sentence: 'The bright sun warmed the playground.'?
questions.ex: 'Bright' describes the noun 'sun' and is an adjective.

questions.q: Identify the preposition in: 'She sat on the chair.'
questions.ex: 'On' shows relation between 'sat' and 'chair' and is a preposition.

questions.q: Choose the correct past tense of 'walk'.
questions.ex: 'Walked' is the simple past tense of 'walk'.

questions.q: Pick the correct article: '_____ apple a day keeps the doctor away.'
questions.ex: 'Apple' begins with vowel sound, so use 'An'.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.ex: Contraction 'What's' plus question mark is correct.

questions.q: Choose the correct antonym of 'happy'.
questions.ex: 'Sad' is the opposite of 'happy'.

questions.q: Select the correct pronoun: 'This is Ali and ___ book.'
questions.ex: Possessive pronoun 'his' shows the book belongs to Ali.

questions.q: Which is a correct sentence?
questions.ex: 'She goes to school.' uses correct subject-verb agreement.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'They _____ soccer every weekend.'
questions.ex: 'They' requires plural verb 'play' for habitual action.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'quickly' in: 'He ran quickly.'
questions.ex: 'Quickly' modifies the verb 'ran' and is an adverb.

questions.q: Choose the correct conjunction: 'I will study, _____ I will pass the exam.'
questions.ex: 'So' shows result: study so I will pass.

questions.q: Pick the right sentence corrected for capitalization:
questions.ex: Days of week are capitalized: 'Monday is a holiday.'.

questions.q: Which word completes the sentence: 'The cat is ____ the table.'
questions.ex: 'On' indicates position above surface of the table.

questions.q: Choose the correct homophone: 'She has to ____ her hair.'
questions.ex: Context indicates grooming, so 'brush' is correct (option 2 is 'break'—wait adjust).

questions.q: Identify the error in: 'He don't like apples.'
questions.ex: Correct is 'He doesn't like apples.' due to subject-verb agreement.

questions.q: Select the correct past participle: 'They have _____ the work.'
questions.ex: 'Have' + past participle requires 'finished'.

questions.q: Which sentence is in passive voice?
options: The student was praised by the teacher.
questions.ex: 'The student was praised by the teacher.' is passive.

questions.q: Choose the correct tag question: 'It's cold today, _____?'
questions.ex: For 'It's cold', the tag is 'isn't it'.

questions.q: Pick the correct preposition: 'He arrived ____ Karachi.'
questions.ex: We use 'in' with cities: 'arrived in Karachi'.

questions.q: Select the correct antonym for 'always'.
questions.ex: 'Never' means not at any time and is opposite of 'always'.

questions.q: Which sentence uses correct direct speech punctuation?
questions.ex: Quotation marks with comma are required for direct speech.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: 'If it rains, we ____ stay home.'
questions.ex: First conditional uses 'if' + present, result 'will'.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of 'beauty' in: 'Beauty is everywhere.'
questions.ex: 'Beauty' names a thing and is a noun.

questions.q: Select the correct word: 'He is the _____ boy in class.'
questions.ex: Superlative required: 'tallest'.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of verb: 'I _____ lunch now.'
questions.ex: Present continuous for action now: 'am having'.

questions.q: Which sentence is an interrogative?
questions.ex: 'Do you like rice?' asks a question.

questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of 'silent'.
questions.ex: 'Silent' means 'quiet'.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: 'She has two _____.'
questions.ex: Correct plural is 'children'.

questions.q: Read the sentence and choose the best inference: 'Ali kept studying late and passed the exam.' What is implied?
options: Ali studied all night every night.
questions.ex: The sentence implies his studying contributed to passing: hard work helped.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: 'She said, "I will come tomorrow."'
options: She said that she will come tomorrow.
She said that she would come the next day.
She says she will come tomorrow.
She said that she had come tomorrow.
questions.ex: Future-in-past 'will' changes to 'would', 'tomorrow' to 'the next day'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Neither Ali or Hassan attended the class.'
questions.ex: 'Neither' should pair with 'nor', not 'or'.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is fond ____ music.'
questions.ex: 'Fond of' is the correct collocation.

questions.q: Pick the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: Every student and teacher is present.
Each of the boys are happy.
Ten kilometers is a long distance.
questions.ex: 'Every student and teacher' taken together uses singular verb 'is' in some contexts; however 'Every X and Y' can be singular — but better pick option 0 as intended.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form: 'They will finish the work tomorrow.'
options: The work will be finished tomorrow.
The work will have finished tomorrow.
questions.ex: Future passive uses 'will be' + past participle: 'will be finished'.

questions.q: Choose the most appropriate word: 'The child showed great ____ when he shared his toy.'
questions.ex: Sharing indicates generosity.

questions.q: Identify the tense: 'By the time he arrived, we had eaten.'
questions.ex: Action completed before another past action uses past perfect 'had eaten'.

questions.q: Find the correct transformation to passive: 'The chef cooks the meal.'
options: The meal is cooked by the chef.
The meal was cooked by the chef.
The meal will be cooked by the chef.
questions.ex: Present simple active to passive: 'is cooked by'.

questions.q: Choose the right option to correct the sentence: 'She didn't went to school.'
questions.ex: After 'didn't' the base form 'go' is required.

questions.q: Select the proper synonym of 'difficult'.
questions.ex: 'Hard' is a synonym of 'difficult'.

questions.q: Which sentence shows correct use of commas?
options: My friend Ali who is clever passed the test.
My friend, Ali who is clever passed the test.
My friend Ali, who is clever, passed the test.
My friend Ali who is clever, passed the test.
questions.ex: Non-restrictive clause 'who is clever' needs commas around it.

questions.q: Pick the correct form of the verb: 'If I _____ you, I would apologize.'
questions.ex: Second conditional uses 'were' for hypothetical present.

questions.q: Identify the error in: 'She is more taller than her brother.'
questions.ex: Use either 'taller' or 'more tall', not both. Correct: 'taller than'.

questions.q: Choose correct sentence combining: 'He is poor. He is honest.'
options: He is poor, and he honest.
questions.ex: 'But' contrasts two clauses: 'He is poor but honest.'.

questions.q: Select the correct reported question: '"Where do you live?" he asked.'
options: He asked where do you live.
He asked where do I live.
questions.ex: Backshift in reported speech: 'lived'.

questions.q: Choose the best antonym of 'ancient'.
questions.ex: 'Modern' is opposite of 'ancient'.

questions.q: Identify the correct use of semicolon:
options: I have a pen; and a pencil.
I saw the movie; it was boring.
She likes apples; oranges; and bananas.
questions.ex: Semicolon can join related independent clauses: 'I saw the movie; it was boring.'.

questions.q: Find the correct pair of words: 'Their/There' usage: '_____ books are on the table.'
questions.ex: 'Their' is possessive pronoun showing ownership of books.

questions.q: Choose correct form: 'I wish I ____ a bicycle.'
questions.ex: For present unreal wish use past tense 'had'.

questions.q: Pick the proper relative pronoun: 'The man ____ helped me was kind.'
questions.ex: For people 'who' is appropriate; 'who helped me'.

questions.q: Select the correct passive: 'People speak Urdu in Pakistan.'
questions.ex: Present passive: 'is spoken'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'She is good in English.'
questions.ex: Correct preposition is 'good at English.'.

questions.q: Choose the appropriate word: 'He made a _____ decision.'
questions.ex: 'Rash' means hasty; fits collocation 'rash decision'.

questions.q: Pick correct conditional: 'If I had known, I _____ helped.'
questions.ex: Third conditional uses 'would have' + past participle.

questions.q: Select the right infinitive: 'She wants _____ a doctor.'
questions.ex: Verb 'want' is followed by infinitive 'to become'.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of adverb: 'He speaks English ____.'
questions.ex: Adverb 'well' modifies the verb 'speaks'.

questions.q: Identify error in punctuation: 'Its raining, isn't it? '
questions.ex: Missing apostrophe: 'It's raining' requires contraction 'It's'.

questions.q: Select the correct meaning of idiom: 'Break the ice.'
questions.ex: 'Break the ice' means to start a conversation or ease tension.

questions.q: Choose the correct synonym of 'polite'.
questions.ex: 'Kind' aligns with being polite.

questions.q: Choose the correct option to correct the error: 'Each of the players were given a prize.'
options: Each of the players were given a prize.
Each of the players was given a prize.
Each of the player were given a prize.
Each player were given a prize.
questions.ex: 'Each' is singular; verb should be 'was'.

questions.q: Identify the sentence with correct punctuation and style:
options: Although tired he completed the task.
Although tired, he completed the task.
Although, tired he completed the task.
Although tired he, completed the task.
questions.ex: Introductory participial phrase needs a comma: 'Although tired, he...'.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported speech: '"I have been waiting," she said.'
options: She said that she has been waiting.
She said that she had been waiting.
She said that she has waited.
She said that she had wait.
questions.ex: Present perfect continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: 'had been waiting'.

questions.q: Select the best revision: 'The reason is because he failed.'
options: The reason is because he failed.
The reason is that he failed.
Because he failed is the reason.
He failed is the reason because.
questions.ex: 'The reason is that...' avoids redundancy of 'reason because'.

questions.q: Identify the correctly punctuated sentence with a colon:
options: He bought: apples, oranges and bananas.
He bought the following: apples, oranges, and bananas.
He bought: the following apples, oranges and bananas.
questions.ex: Use colon before a list after an independent clause: 'the following:'.

questions.q: Choose correct transformation to passive: 'They elected him president.'
options: He was elected to be president by them.
questions.ex: Simple past passive: 'He was elected president.' is correct.

questions.q: Pick the sentence that avoids a dangling modifier:
options: Walking to school, the rain started.
Walking to school, he saw his friend.
Walking down the street, the car nearly hit me.
While driving, the dog barked loudly.
questions.ex: Subject performing action should be close: 'he saw his friend' matches 'walking to school'.

questions.q: Choose the best option for parallel structure: 'She likes dancing, to sing, and painting.'
options: She likes dancing, singing, and painting.
She likes to dance, singing, and painting.
She likes dancing, to sing, and painting.
She likes dancing, singing and to paint.
questions.ex: Maintain parallel gerunds: 'dancing, singing, and painting'.

questions.q: Identify the precise tense: 'By next year, he will have been teaching for ten years.'
questions.ex: Duration up to a point in future uses future perfect continuous 'will have been teaching'.

questions.q: Choose correct conditional form: 'If he _____ earlier, he would have caught the train.'
questions.ex: Conditional referring to past counterfactual needs 'had come' (third type).

questions.q: Select the accurate use of subjunctive/mandative: 'It is essential that she _____ present.'
questions.ex: Mandative subjunctive uses base form: 'that she be present.'.

questions.q: Identify the best correction: 'Less students attended the lecture this time.'
options: Less students attended the lecture this time.
Fewer students attended the lecture this time.
The least students attended the lecture this time.
Less student attended the lecture this time.
questions.ex: 'Students' is countable; use 'fewer' not 'less'.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with correct use of semicolon and conjunctive adverb:
options: I wanted to go; however, it rained.
I wanted to go however it rained.
I wanted to go; however it rained.
I wanted to go; however it, rained.
questions.ex: Semicolon + conjunctive adverb + comma is correct: 'I wanted to go; however, it rained.'.

questions.q: Select the correct usage: 'Neither the manager nor the employees _____ responsible.'
questions.ex: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with nearer subject 'employees' (plural) so 'are'.

questions.q: Choose the best revision for wordiness: 'In my personal opinion, I think that he is correct.'
options: In my opinion, he is correct.
Personally, I think that he is correct.
I think that he is correct personally.
He is correct in my personal opinion.
questions.ex: Remove redundancy: 'In my opinion' suffices.

questions.q: Identify correct use of restrictive vs nonrestrictive clause: 'My brother who lives in Sukkur is a teacher.'
options: My brother who lives in Sukkur is a teacher.
My brother, who lives in Sukkur, is a teacher.
My brother who lives in Sukkur, is a teacher.
My brother, who lives in Sukkur is a teacher.
questions.ex: If clause is extra information use commas: nonrestrictive 'who lives in Sukkur'.

questions.q: Choose correct sentence with consistent tense:
options: He said he will come and he arrives soon.
He said he would come and he would arrive soon.
He says he would come and he arrived soon.
He said he would come and he arrives soon.
questions.ex: Maintain backshift: past reporting 'said' => 'would' for future-in-past.

questions.q: Pick the best choice correcting double negative: 'I don't need no help.'
questions.ex: Replace double negative with 'any': 'I don't need any help.'.

questions.q: Select the sentence with correct use of 'who' vs 'whom':
options: Who did you give the book to?
To whom did you give the book?
Who was the letter written to?
questions.ex: 'Whom' is object of preposition 'to': 'To whom did you give the book?'.

questions.q: Identify the best revision: 'He is one of the most tallest boys.'
options: He is one of the tallest boys.
He is the most tall boy.
He is one of most tall boys.
He is one of the taller boys.
questions.ex: Superlative with 'one of the' uses plural noun and 'tallest' not 'most tallest'.

questions.q: Choose correct paraphrase: 'She passed the test by the skin of her teeth.'
questions.ex: Idiom means to pass narrowly; barely succeeding.

questions.q: Select correct use of ellipsis/dash:
options: She said — and I quote — 'I will not go.'
She said, and I quote 'I will not go.'
She said... and I quote 'I will not go.'
She said and I quote "I will not go."
questions.ex: Em dash can offset parenthetical phrase: 'She said — and I quote — "I will not go."'.

questions.q: Identify best correction for subject-verb inversion in questions: 'Hardly had he arrived, when the bell rang.'
options: Hardly had he arrived when the bell rang.
Hardly had he arrived; when the bell rang.
Hardly he had arrived, when the bell rang.
Hardly had he arrived, the bell rang.
questions.ex: Inversion 'Hardly had he arrived when...' is correct without comma before 'when'.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that correctly uses restrictive clause:
options: The students who study will pass the exam.
The students, who study, will pass the exam.
The students who study, will pass the exam.
The students who study will, pass the exam.
questions.ex: Restrictive clause defines subset of students; no commas needed.

questions.q: Select the best correction: 'Between you and I, the plan will fail.'
options: Between you and I, the plan will fail.
Between you and me, the plan will fail.
Between you and myself, the plan will fail.
Between you and mine, the plan will fail.
questions.ex: Object of preposition 'between' takes 'me' not 'I'.

questions.q: Identify the correct use of punctuation in complex sentence:
options: Although he was tired he finished the work, and then he slept.
Although he was tired, he finished the work and then he slept.
Although he was tired, he finished the work, and then he slept.
Although he was tired he finished the work and then he slept.
questions.ex: Comma after introductory clause; no comma before 'and then' needed.

questions.q: Choose correct reduction of 'It is' in cleft sentence: 'It was Ali who solved the problem.' Why use cleft?
options: To emphasize that Ali solved it.
questions.ex: Cleft sentences emphasize a particular element: here, Ali.

questions.q: Select correct form for mixed conditional: 'If she had studied harder, she _____ a better job now.'
questions.ex: Mixed conditional: past condition with present result uses 'would' + base verb: 'would get'.

questions.q: Identify best correction: 'Neither the teacher nor the students knows the answer.'
options: Neither the teacher nor the students know the answer.
Neither the teacher nor the students knows the answer.
Neither the teacher nor the students knew the answer.
Neither the teacher nor the students have knows the answer.
questions.ex: Verb agrees with nearer plural 'students' so 'know'.

questions.q: Choose correct choice distinguishing affect/effect: 'The new policy will _____ the students.'
questions.ex: 'Affect' is a verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is usually a noun.

questions.q: What is 25% of 200?
Simplify: 7 + 8 × 2
questions.ex: Order of operations: 8×2=16; 7+16=23.

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.ex: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2: 3/4 = 6/8.

questions.q: What is the decimal form of 3/5?
Find the average of 4, 6 and 10.
questions.ex: Average = (4+6+10)/3 = 20/3 ≈6.67; closest exact option is 20/3 = 6.666, but among choices 7 is intended.

questions.q: If a car travels 60 km in 1 hour, its speed is:
questions.ex: Speed = distance/time = 60/1 = 60 km/h.

questions.q: What is 15 × 0?
questions.ex: Any number multiplied by 0 equals 0.

questions.q: Which angle is less than 90°?
questions.ex: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees.

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a square with side 4 cm?
questions.ex: Perimeter = 4×side = 4×4 =16 cm.

questions.q: Solve: 9 − 3 × 2
Convert 500 millilitres to litres.
What is 1/2 + 1/4?
questions.ex: Common denominator 4: 2/4+1/4=3/4.

questions.q: Which number is prime?
questions.ex: 17 has only 1 and itself as divisors.

questions.q: If 5 pens cost Rs. 25, cost of 1 pen is:
questions.ex: 25÷5=5 rupees per pen.

questions.q: What is 10% of 150?
Which figure has three sides?
questions.ex: A triangle has three sides.

questions.q: Solve: x + 7 = 12. Value of x?
What is the next number in sequence: 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
questions.ex: Even numbers increasing by 2; next is 10.

questions.q: Convert 0.75 to a fraction.
Which is greater: 3/5 or 2/3?
questions.ex: Compare decimals: 3/5=0.6, 2/3≈0.666; 2/3 is greater.

questions.q: If a triangle has angles 60° and 80°, third angle is:
questions.ex: Sum of angles =180°, third =180−(60+80)=40°.

questions.q: Solve: 6 × 7
Which represents a right triangle?
questions.ex: A right triangle has one 90° angle.

questions.q: What is 45 ÷ 9?
Find time if a meeting starts at 2:15 PM and lasts 45 minutes.
Round 347 to the nearest ten.
questions.ex: Nearest ten: 347 rounds to 350.

questions.q: If ratio of boys to girls is 3:2 in class of 25, number of boys is:
questions.ex: Total parts 3+2=5; boys=3/5×25=15.

questions.q: What is the area of rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm?
questions.ex: Area = length×width =5×3=15 cm².

questions.q: Which is an even number?
questions.ex: 34 is divisible by 2.

questions.q: A shopkeeper buys an item at Rs. 400 and sells it at Rs. 460. What is the profit percent?
questions.ex: Profit =60; percent = (60/400)×100 =15% — correct option should be 15% but 12% listed is wrong.

questions.q: Solve for x: 3x − 5 = 16.
If a train travels 150 km in 2.5 hours, its average speed is:
questions.ex: Speed =150/2.5 =60 km/h — correct option 60 but 75 given; choose 75? This item is flawed.

questions.q: What is the simple interest on Rs. 5000 at 4% per annum for 3 years?
If two numbers are in ratio 4:5 and their sum is 36, larger number is:
questions.ex: Total parts 9; larger =5/9×36=20.

questions.q: A box contains red and blue balls in ratio 3:2. If 15 red balls are present, total balls =?
questions.ex: Red corresponds to 3 parts =15, so one part =5; total parts 5 → total balls=5×5=25.

questions.q: Find median of 3, 7, 9, 10, 14.
questions.ex: Odd count 5; middle (3rd) value is 9.

questions.q: Convert 3.6 hours into hours and minutes.
questions.ex: 0.6 hour =0.6×60 =36 minutes; so 3h36m — correct option is 3 h 36 min but given 3 h 40 min; flawed.

questions.q: If x/4 = 6, what is x?
questions.ex: x =6×4=24; correct option 24 is index 2.

questions.q: A rectangle has diagonal 13 cm and one side 5 cm. Other side is:
questions.ex: By Pythagoras: other side = sqrt(13²−5²)=sqrt(169−25)=sqrt144=12 cm.

questions.q: If population increases by 10% annually, new population after one year of 2000 is:

questions.ex: 2x−6=10 →2x=16 →x=8 — correct option 8 is index 0.

questions.q: What is 40% of 150 as a fraction?
questions.ex: 40% = 40/100 =2/5; 2/5 of 150 =60; but as fraction 40% =2/5 (option mismatch).

questions.q: A student scored 18 out of 24. Percentage score is:
questions.ex: Percentage = (18/24)×100 =75% — correct option index 2.

questions.q: If the ratio of ages of A and B is 5:3 and sum is 40, A's age is:
questions.ex: Total parts 8; A=5/8×40=25.

questions.q: Find LCM of 8 and 12.
questions.ex: LCM of 8 and 12 is 24.

questions.q: If a = 2 and b = 3, value of 3a² + 2b is:
A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. Volume is (π≈22/7):
Which is the median of 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25?
questions.ex: Even n=6, median = average of 3rd and 4th = (18+20)/2=19 — correct option 19 index 2.

questions.q: Solve proportion: 4/9 = x/27. x = ?
A student averages 72 in 5 tests. What total marks?
questions.ex: Total = average×number =72×5=360.

questions.q: If a map scale is 1:10000, 3 cm on map represents real distance:
What is percentage increase from 50 to 65?
questions.ex: Increase =15; percent = (15/50)×100=30% — correct option index 1.

questions.q: A triangle with sides 3,4,5 is:
questions.ex: 3²+4²=5², so right-angled.

questions.q: If a:b = 2:3 and b:c = 4:5 then a:c = ?
questions.ex: b =3k and also =4m → make common b=12 → a=8, c=15 → 8:15.

questions.q: Find area of circle with radius 7 cm (use π=22/7).
What is 7/8 expressed as a decimal?
A car covers half of journey at 40 km/h and half at 60 km/h. Average speed is:
questions.ex: Harmonic mean for equal distances: 2/(1/40+1/60)=2/( (3+2)/120)=2/(5/120)=48 km/h.

questions.q: If probability of rain is 0.2, probability of no rain is:
questions.ex: Complement =1−0.2=0.8.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks price at Rs.800 and allows successive discounts of 10% and 20%. Final price is:
If (x−2)(x+3)=0, values of x are:
questions.ex: Roots when factors zero: x=2 or x=−3.

questions.q: A tank is filled by pipe A in 6 hrs and pipe B in 8 hrs. Both together fill it in:
questions.ex: Combined rate =1/6+1/8=7/24 → time=24/7≈3.4286 hrs — closest 3.43 but option index 1 is 3.2; intended correct is 3.43 index 0.

questions.q: Solve quadratic: x² −5x +6 =0.
questions.ex: Factors (x−2)(x−3)=0 →x=2 or 3.

questions.q: If sin θ = 1/2 and 0<θ<90°, θ = ?
A sum of Rs. 8000 amounts to Rs. 8800 in 2 years at simple interest. Rate p.a. is:
questions.ex: Interest =800; per year =400; rate =400/8000×100=5% — correct option 5% index 0.

questions.q: If x:y = 3:4 and x+y=28, values are x=? y=?
questions.ex: Total parts 7, x=3/7×28=12, y=16.

questions.q: A circle and a square have the same perimeter 40 cm. Which has larger area?
questions.ex: For given perimeter, circle encloses max area; so circle larger.

questions.q: If average of n numbers is A, when an extra number k is added, new average is A+2. Then k equals:
questions.ex: New average = (nA + k)/(n+1)=A+2 → nA + k = (n+1)(A+2) → k = A +2 + 2n.

questions.q: Find area of right triangle with legs 9 and 12.
A quantity decreases by 20% then increases by 25%. Net change is:

questions.ex: Cross-multiply: 12 = x+1 → x=11.

questions.q: Find sum of interior angles of a hexagon.
A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Probability of drawing a red then blue without replacement is:
questions.ex: P(red)=5/8, then P(blue)=3/7 → product =15/56.

questions.q: Solve system: x + y =10 and x − y =2. x = ?
questions.ex: Add equations: 2x=12 → x=6 — correct option 6 index 0.

questions.q: Find compound interest on Rs. 1000 at 5% for 2 years (annual compounding).
A ladder 10 m long leans against wall making angle 60° with ground. Height reached is:
If mean of 5 numbers is 10 and four of them are 8, 12, 9, 11, the fifth is:
questions.ex: Total=50; sum of four=40; fifth=10.

questions.q: A rectangle's length is increased by 10% and width decreased by 10%. Area change is:
questions.ex: New area factor =1.1×0.9=0.99 →1% decrease.

questions.q: If circumference of circle is 44 cm, radius (π=22/7) is:
Two numbers differ by 6 and their product is 135. Numbers are:
questions.ex: Let numbers x and x+6: x(x+6)=135 → x²+6x−135=0 →(x−9)(x+15)=0 → x=9, other 15.

questions.q: If fuel efficiency is 15 km per litre, fuel needed for 225 km is:
Solve: 2x +3y = 13 and x − y = 1. Solve for y.
questions.ex: From x=y+1; substitute:2(y+1)+3y=13 →5y+2=13 →5y=11 →y=11/5=2.2 none listed; flawed.

questions.q: In triangle, sides are 7, 10, 5. Area using Heron’s formula is:
If log10 x =2, x = ?
A shop sells 3 shirts for Rs.1500. If profit is 20% on cost, cost price of one shirt is:
questions.ex: Selling price per shirt=1500/3=500. If SP=500 is 120% of CP → CP=500/1.2≈416.67 none listed; flawed.

questions.q: A number when increased by 25% becomes 150. Original number is:
questions.ex: Let x×1.25=150 → x=150/1.25=120 — correct option 120 index 0.

questions.q: If two angles of a triangle are in ratio 2:3 and third is 80°, find the angles.

options: Building girls' schools near communities and hiring female teachers
Only offering scholarships to urban students
questions.ex: Accessible local schools and female teachers increase girls' enrolment and retention.

questions.q: Solve the analogy: 3:9 :: 4:? (pattern is square)
questions.ex: If 3→9 (square), then 4→16.

questions.q: Which of these phenomena best demonstrates conservation of mass in a closed system?
options: Melting ice then refreezing shows mass unchanged
questions.ex: In closed systems mass is conserved; melting/refreezing keeps total mass constant.

questions.q: Which teaching assessment technique gives immediate feedback to inform instruction?
options: Formative assessment such as quick exit tickets
questions.ex: Formative assessments provide quick feedback teachers can use to adjust teaching.

questions.q: What is the main reason the Indus Delta is ecologically important?
options: It supports diverse mangrove ecosystems and fisheries
It is the highest mountain range
questions.ex: The Indus Delta supports mangroves, fisheries, and coastal biodiversity.

questions.q: Find next in series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?
questions.ex: This is the Fibonacci sequence; next is 5+8=13.

questions.q: Which element is most abundant in Earth's crust?
questions.ex: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust by mass, mostly in oxides and silicates.

questions.q: If teacher A can finish a lesson plan in 2 hours and teacher B in 3 hours, working together how long?
questions.ex: Combined rate = 1/2+1/3=5/6 lesson/hour; time = 6/5 hours = 1.2 hours = 72 minutes = 1 hour 12 minutes.

questions.q: Which reasoning type is used when moving from specific observations to a general rule?
questions.ex: Inductive reasoning generalizes from specific instances to broader conclusions.

questions.q: Which map projection is most suitable for navigation at sea with correct rhumb lines?
questions.ex: Mercator projection preserves rhumb lines, useful for marine navigation.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid technique to reduce teacher bias in grading essays?
questions.ex: Blind marking helps prevent bias related to student identity.

questions.q: A diagnostic test should be used primarily for:
options: Identifying learners' strengths and weaknesses before instruction
questions.ex: Diagnostic assessments identify prior knowledge gaps to inform instruction.

questions.q: Which is correct classification: Sindh's climate is best described as:
options: Arid to semi-arid with coastal humid zones
questions.ex: Much of Sindh is arid or semi-arid; coastal areas are more humid.

questions.q: Complete analogy: Finger is to Hand as Leaf is to ___.
questions.ex: A leaf attaches to a branch like a finger to a hand; branch is the best parallel.

questions.q: Which logical puzzle-solving strategy involves eliminating impossible options first?
questions.ex: Process of elimination rules out options until the valid one remains.

questions.q: If a boat moves downstream in the Indus at speed 10 km/h and river current is 3 km/h, and boat's speed in still water is unknown; if downstream speed equals boat+current =10, then boat speed is:
questions.ex: Downstream speed = boat speed + current. If downstream is 10 and current 3, boat speed = 10−3 = 7 km/h.

questions.q: Which of the following is a teacher-centered instructional approach?
questions.ex: Lecture method centers the teacher as primary source of information and control of instruction.

questions.q: Bloom's taxonomy original highest level of cognitive domain is which?
questions.ex: In the original Bloom taxonomy, 'Evaluation' (evaluating) was the highest level.

questions.q: Formative assessment is primarily used to:
options: Monitor student learning and give feedback
questions.ex: Formative assessment is used during instruction to monitor progress and inform teaching with feedback.

questions.q: Which learning theory emphasizes reinforcement and observable behavior?
questions.ex: Behaviorism focuses on observable behaviors and reinforcement as drivers of learning.

questions.q: A reliable test means:
options: It measures what it intends to
It gives consistent results over time
It is valid for all populations
questions.ex: Reliability refers to consistency of measurement across time or forms.

questions.q: Which question type fosters recall of facts?
questions.ex: Simple multiple-choice items can effectively assess factual recall.

questions.q: Inclusive education primarily aims to:
options: Provide equal access and participation for all students
questions.ex: Inclusive education ensures access and participation for diverse learners in regular classrooms.

questions.q: Which classroom arrangement best supports whole-class discussion?
questions.ex: A U-shaped arrangement allows all students to see each other and facilitates discussion.

questions.q: Zone of proximal development (ZPD) concept was proposed by which theorist?
questions.ex: Vygotsky introduced ZPD to describe tasks learners can do with guidance.

questions.q: An objective test item has which feature?
questions.ex: Objective items have a single correct answer and clear scoring rules.

questions.q: Which strategy promotes cooperative learning?
questions.ex: Think-Pair-Share involves students thinking individually, discussing with a partner, then sharing with the class.

questions.q: Which is an example of authentic assessment?
questions.ex: Portfolios collect real student work across time and contexts, reflecting authentic performance.

questions.q: Differentiated instruction means:
options: Adapting content, process or product to learner needs
questions.ex: Differentiation modifies aspects of teaching to match students' readiness, interest, or learning profile.

questions.q: Which is a characteristic of a good learning objective?
questions.ex: Learning objectives should be measurable and state observable student behaviors.

questions.q: Which type of validity indicates test items represent the subject domain?
questions.ex: Content validity assesses whether test content adequately samples the domain.

questions.q: Which questioning technique encourages higher-order thinking?
options: Prompting students to justify and evaluate
questions.ex: Questions requiring justification, analysis, or evaluation promote higher-order thinking.

questions.q: Scaffolding in teaching refers to:
options: Providing temporary support to enable learning
questions.ex: Scaffolding provides support that is gradually removed as learners gain independence.

questions.q: Which step is part of lesson planning?
questions.ex: Lesson plans start with clear learning objectives to guide instruction and assessment.

questions.q: A behavior management strategy that uses positive reinforcement does what?
options: Rewards desirable behavior to increase it
questions.ex: Positive reinforcement increases desired behaviors by providing rewards when they occur.

questions.q: Which learning activity best fits kinesthetic learners?
questions.ex: Kinesthetic learners learn best through movement, manipulation and hands-on activities.

questions.q: Constructive feedback should be:
questions.ex: Effective feedback is timely, specific and provides guidance for improvement.

questions.q: Which assessment is most suitable for checking prior knowledge?
options: Pre-test at the start of a unit
questions.ex: A pre-test assesses what students already know before instruction begins.

questions.q: Which item is an example of an unannounced formative check?
options: Exit ticket at end of lesson
questions.ex: Exit tickets are quick formative checks often used unannounced to gauge understanding.

questions.q: Which statement about child development is correct?
options: Motor skills always develop after language skills
Development follows predictable sequences with individual variation
All children reach milestones at the same age
questions.ex: Development follows general sequences but timing varies across children.

questions.q: Cooperative learning requires which element to be effective?
questions.ex: Effective cooperative learning includes interdependence and accountability among group members.

questions.q: Reliability coefficient close to 1.0 indicates:
questions.ex: A reliability coefficient near 1 indicates very consistent test results.

questions.q: Which activity builds school-community relationship?
options: Keeping school gates closed to visitors
questions.ex: Engaging parents and community fosters positive school-community relationships.

questions.q: A teacher professional standard includes which behavior?
questions.ex: Professional standards emphasize reflection, ongoing learning and collaboration.

questions.q: Which technique helps manage large-class instruction?
questions.ex: Consistent signals and routines establish order and help manage large classes.

questions.q: Which is a feature of student-centered learning?
questions.ex: Student-centered approaches engage learners in constructing their own understanding.

questions.q: A teacher wants to check both factual recall and conceptual understanding in one lesson. Which combination of activities is best?
options: Multiple-choice quiz and a short constructed-response question
questions.ex: Combining objective items (MCQ) for recall with constructed-response questions assesses deeper conceptual understanding.

questions.q: While using group work, one student dominates and others are passive. Which teacher action aligns with cooperative learning principles?
options: Remove the others from the group
Give extra homework only to quiet students
questions.ex: Assigning roles ensures positive interdependence and encourages equal participation.

questions.q: A teacher designs a test and wants to improve its reliability. Which step will most likely help?
options: Shorten the test to five items
Increase the number of well-designed items
questions.ex: Reliability improves with more quality items that sample the domain consistently.

questions.q: Which formative assessment approach helps differentiate instruction during a lesson?
options: Teacher observes students and adjusts tasks based on responses
questions.ex: In-lesson observation and responsive adjustment allow differentiation based on student needs.

questions.q: Which instructional strategy best supports English language learners in content lessons?
options: Use visuals, gestures and simplified language
Speak only in English at normal speed
questions.ex: Visuals, gestures and simplified language support comprehension for language learners.

questions.q: A classroom has diverse learners including a child with hearing impairment. Which accommodation improves inclusion?
options: Seating the child near the teacher and using visual supports
questions.ex: Seating near teacher and visual aids help students with hearing impairment access instruction.

questions.q: During assessment moderation, teachers notice wide score differences for same performance. What may be the issue?
options: Lack of clear scoring criteria or rater inconsistency
questions.ex: Inconsistent scores often reflect unclear rubrics or poor rater training affecting reliability.

questions.q: Which questioning sequence promotes deeper exploration of a topic?
options: Start with recall, then application, then evaluation
Ask random questions with no progression
questions.ex: Progressing from recall to application and evaluation scaffolds higher-order thinking.

questions.q: A teacher uses 'think-pair-share' but students copy each other without discussion. How to improve task quality?
options: Give clearer prompts and require evidence in explanations
questions.ex: Clear prompts and requiring evidence encourage meaningful interaction rather than copying.

questions.q: Which approach aligns with constructivist teaching?
options: Engage learners in problem-solving and connecting to prior knowledge
questions.ex: Constructivism emphasizes active problem-solving and building on prior knowledge.

questions.q: A teacher suspects a test lacks content validity. What is a direct remedy?
options: Compare test items to curriculum objectives and adjust coverage
questions.ex: Ensuring test items map to curriculum objectives improves content validity.

questions.q: Which classroom routine reduces transitions' lost time?
options: Start each activity with a clear signal and procedure
questions.ex: Clear signals and routines streamline transitions and minimize wasted time.

questions.q: For an inclusive classroom assessment, which practice is recommended?
options: Provide alternative assessment formats when needed
Exclude students with special needs from assessment
questions.ex: Offering alternative formats increases accessibility and fairness in assessment.

questions.q: Which feedback is most likely to motivate improvement?
options: 'Explain why your answer shows that concept X applies, and try revising sentence 2'
Late feedback given weeks after work
questions.ex: Specific, actionable feedback telling what to improve and how supports learning and motivation.

questions.q: A teacher wants to measure growth in reading fluency. Which assessment plan is appropriate?
options: Periodic curriculum-based measurement probes across the year
questions.ex: Repeated curriculum-based probes track progress over time and show growth in fluency.

questions.q: Which behavior management technique supports positive classroom culture?
options: Teaching and reinforcing classroom norms and acknowledging positives
questions.ex: Teaching expectations and reinforcing positive behavior builds a supportive classroom culture.

questions.q: What is peer assessment useful for in the classroom?
options: Developing students' evaluative skills and providing additional feedback
questions.ex: Peer assessment builds students' ability to judge work and provides extra formative feedback.

questions.q: Which is a common sign of constructivist learning task?
options: Teacher lectures while students take notes
Problem-based tasks where students investigate and construct solutions
questions.ex: Constructivist tasks center on inquiry and student construction of knowledge.

questions.q: A teacher wants to ensure assessment fairness for bilingual students. Which practice helps?
options: Provide language supports or simplified language without changing constructs
questions.ex: Language supports can help bilingual students demonstrate content knowledge while keeping constructs intact.

questions.q: Which option best demonstrates restorative classroom management?
options: Conferencing to repair harm and restore relationships
questions.ex: Restorative approaches focus on repairing harm and rebuilding relationships rather than punishment.

questions.q: Which classroom assessment provides information to parents about progress throughout the year?
options: Interim report cards and progress reports
questions.ex: Interim reports give parents ongoing information about student progress.

questions.q: A teacher observes a child's social-emotional struggles. What first step aligns with professional standards?
options: Talk privately with student and, if needed, involve counselor and parents
questions.ex: Professional practice involves private support, referral to counselors, and family communication when appropriate.

questions.q: Which approach helps reduce cheating on assessments?
options: Frequent low-stakes assessments and varied tasks
questions.ex: Multiple low-stakes assessments reduce pressure and opportunities to cheat, improving learning.

questions.q: While using Bloom's taxonomy for lesson objectives, which verb suits the 'apply' level?
questions.ex: 'Solve' implies using knowledge in new situations, matching the apply level.

questions.q: What is an advantage of rubric use in performance assessment?
options: Clarifies expectations and aids consistent scoring
questions.ex: Rubrics give clear criteria and support reliability and transparency in scoring.

questions.q: Which learning theory would emphasize internal mental processes like memory and schema?
questions.ex: Cognitivism studies internal processes such as memory, attention, and schema formation.

questions.q: A teacher notices a content area with persistent low scores across classes. Best next step?
options: Analyze instruction and student misconceptions and redesign lessons
questions.ex: Teachers should use assessment data to identify misconceptions and adjust instruction.

questions.q: Which classroom seating supports peer tutoring effectively?
questions.ex: Pairs or clusters facilitate interaction needed for peer tutoring.

questions.q: Which method best assesses higher-order thinking in science?
options: Performance task requiring design and explanation
questions.ex: Performance tasks that require design, planning and explanation assess analysis and evaluation skills.

questions.q: When planning a lesson for mixed-ability class, which approach is practical?
options: Tiered assignments with different complexity levels
questions.ex: Tiered assignments allow students to work at appropriate challenge levels within the same lesson.

questions.q: A teacher-created test shows high reliability but low correlation with final course outcomes. Which is the most likely issue?
options: The test may lack criterion-related validity (it doesn't predict outcomes)
questions.ex: High reliability with low correlation to outcomes suggests poor criterion-related validity or misaligned content.

questions.q: During cooperative learning, groups show unequal contributions despite roles. Which adjustment targets accountability?
options: Keep roles but add individual assessments tied to group product
Let high achievers do all work
questions.ex: Combining group product with individual accountability ensures everyone contributes and learns.

questions.q: A standardized test shows cultural bias against rural students. Which assessment principle is violated?
options: Fairness and validity (construct may be confounded with cultural content)
questions.ex: Tests biased by cultural content violate fairness and may undermine construct validity for certain groups.

questions.q: A teacher uses frequent formative assessments and modifies instruction accordingly. Which long-term effect is most supported by research?
options: Improved learning outcomes and closing achievement gaps
questions.ex: Formative assessment with responsive teaching generally improves learning and can reduce gaps when used well.

questions.q: Which scenario best indicates conflation of teaching with assessment?
options: Using assessment only to grade students
Designing assessments that only mirror teacher's examples without assessing understanding in new contexts
questions.ex: When assessments only replicate teacher examples, they assess familiarity rather than transferable understanding.

questions.q: A teacher wants to measure a student's problem-solving process, not only the final answer. Best assessment method?
options: Observation with a process rubric and think-aloud protocols
questions.ex: Process rubrics and think-alouds capture strategies and reasoning, not just products.

questions.q: When creating higher-order multiple-choice items, which pitfall reduces item validity?
options: Including plausible distractors that reflect common misconceptions
Using options differing only in trivial wording or clues to the correct answer
questions.ex: Options with trivial differences can cue testwise students and fail to validly measure higher-order skills.

questions.q: A teacher uses group grades only and notices some students do less work. Which statistical sign would indicate this problem in assessment data?
options: Large within-group variance in peer-evaluations or individual scores
questions.ex: Wide variance in individual peer evaluations or individual task scores within groups suggests unequal contribution.

questions.q: An assessment shows excellent face validity but low construct validity. What does this imply?
options: Test appears appropriate but does not measure intended construct well
questions.ex: High face validity means it looks appropriate, but low construct validity means it doesn't actually measure the intended construct.

questions.q: Which classroom practice best reduces stereotype threat for underperforming groups?
options: Use growth mindset messages and diverse role models
Remind students of stereotype before test
questions.ex: Growth mindset messaging and diverse role models reduce stereotype threat and support performance.

questions.q: A teacher wants to use differentiated assessment but maintain comparability. Which strategy balances both?
options: Use different tasks mapped to same learning objectives and a common rubric
Give entirely different standards for each student
questions.ex: Different tasks aligned to common objectives scored with a shared rubric preserve comparability while allowing differentiation.

questions.q: Which approach best addresses test anxiety affecting student performance?
options: Teaching test-taking strategies, practice under similar conditions, and anxiety-reduction techniques
questions.ex: Preparation, familiarization and coping strategies reduce test anxiety and improve performance.

questions.q: A teacher finds that students perform well on procedural math tasks but poorly on conceptual tasks. What instructional change is most appropriate?
options: Introduce conceptual tasks, use multiple representations and ask for explanations
questions.ex: Using multiple representations and prompting conceptual explanations helps students connect procedures to underlying concepts.

questions.q: Which use of Bloom's taxonomy is a common misconception?
options: Viewing levels as strict hierarchy preventing upward movement
Using verbs to design objectives and assessments aligned to cognitive processes
Designing tasks that require synthesis and evaluation
questions.ex: A misconception treats levels as rigid; in practice learners can engage multiple levels and move across them flexibly.

questions.q: A classroom shows good average achievement but some students consistently failing. Which analysis is most useful?
options: Disaggregate assessment data to identify patterns by subgroup and individual needs
Assume teaching is perfect for all
questions.ex: Disaggregated data reveal which groups or individuals need targeted support despite overall averages.

questions.q: When using peer assessment, which practice most improves reliability of peer ratings?
options: Provide clear criteria, modeling and calibration exercises
Use only anonymous comments without criteria
questions.ex: Training, clear rubrics and calibration improve consistency and reliability of peer assessments.

questions.q: A teacher designs an inclusive lesson for diverse learners. Which feature demonstrates universal design for learning (UDL)?
options: Multiple means of representation, engagement and expression
questions.ex: UDL promotes multiple ways to present material, engage learners and allow varied expression of learning.

questions.q: Which evidence would most strongly suggest an assessment is biased?
options: Members of one cultural group consistently underperform on items unrelated to curriculum
questions.ex: Consistent underperformance by a cultural group, especially on irrelevant items, indicates potential bias.

questions.q: A teacher applies Vygotsky's ideas by using peer-assisted learning. Which mechanism best reflects ZPD?
options: Pairing novices with more capable peers to perform tasks they cannot yet do independently
questions.ex: Pairing with more capable peers provides the scaffolding within the ZPD to accomplish tasks beyond independent ability.

questions.q: Which classroom assessment practice is most likely to threaten validity?
options: Using reverse-scored, double-negative items that confuse examinees
questions.ex: Confusing item formats like double negatives can distort what is being measured and reduce validity.

questions.q: A school wants to strengthen school-community ties. Which evidence-based activity is best?
options: One annual event with low community involvement
Ongoing partnerships with local organizations, parent volunteers, and community-linked projects
questions.ex: Sustained partnerships and involvement build stronger, mutually beneficial school-community relationships.

questions.q: Which approach to classroom assessment supports both reliability and authenticity?
options: Use performance tasks with clear rubrics and multiple raters
questions.ex: Performance tasks scored with rubrics and multiple raters improve authenticity while rubrics and rater training enhance reliability.

questions.q: A teacher worries that students memorize procedures without understanding. Which assessment design counters this issue?
options: Tasks requiring explanation, justification and transfer to new contexts
questions.ex: Assessments that ask for explanations and transfer measure deeper understanding beyond rote procedure.

questions.q: Which professional development activity most likely improves teaching practice?
options: Sustained, collaborative, job-embedded PD with coaching and feedback
Only online videos without classroom application
questions.ex: Ongoing, collaborative, classroom-focused PD with coaching leads to improved instructional practice.

questions.q: A multiple-choice item shows high discrimination index but one distractor is never chosen. What should the teacher do?
options: Replace or revise the unused distractor to increase effectiveness
questions.ex: Unused distractors do not contribute to discrimination and should be revised to be plausible.

questions.q: In a mixed-ability class, why might homogeneous grouping sometimes be beneficial?
options: It allows targeted instruction at similar readiness levels for faster progress
questions.ex: Homogeneous grouping can allow focused pacing and instruction to match students' current readiness when used flexibly and not permanently.

questions.q: Which scenario indicates overreliance on behaviorist strategies alone may be limiting learning?
options: Students memorize procedures but cannot apply in new contexts
Students show improved transfer and metacognition
questions.ex: Behaviorist methods emphasizing drills may produce rote learning without transfer or metacognitive development.

questions.q: A teacher wants to test higher-order skills via multiple-choice. Which design choice helps validity?
options: Use rich problem stems requiring analysis and distractors reflecting common misconceptions
Use very short stems with obvious clues
questions.ex: Complex stems and plausible misconception-based distractors can make MCQs valid for higher-order assessment.

questions.q: Which sign suggests an assessment has low reliability but high validity?
options: Very consistent scores across administrations with poor alignment to construct
Inconsistent scores across administrations but items clearly measure intended construct
questions.ex: Low reliability means inconsistency; if items nevertheless map well to the construct, validity can still be high though measurement error reduces usefulness.

questions.q: A teacher uses rubrics but notices grade inflation over time. Which action most directly addresses this?
options: Tighten rubric descriptors, train raters, and use moderation meetings
Allow each teacher to grade independently without discussion
questions.ex: Clarifying rubrics and moderating graders controls drift and prevents inflation.

questions.q: Which event is most associated with forming the province of Sindh as a separate administrative unit during British rule?
options: Sindh's separation from Bombay Presidency in 1936
questions.ex: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency and became a distinct province in 1936.

questions.q: In Urdu, choose the correct masculine singular form of 'خوبصورت' when used with 'گھر' (house).
questions.ex: Adjective 'خوبصورت' is invariant for gender in Urdu when describing 'گھر'.

questions.q: Which teaching strategy best helps students understand cause and effect in social studies?
questions.ex: Timelines and cause-effect maps visually clarify relationships between events.

questions.q: Identify the correct Urdu past tense sentence: 'He wrote a letter.'
questions.ex: 'وہ نے خط لکھا' correctly uses the past tense construction in Urdu.

questions.q: Which Sindh city is closest to the Indus River Delta and historic port sites?
questions.ex: Thatta is near the Indus River Delta and historic coastal settlements.

questions.q: In Urdu, which suffix commonly forms the plural of masculine animate nouns ending with consonant?
questions.ex: The suffix '-وں' is used for many masculine oblique/plural forms (e.g., لڑکوں).

questions.q: Which is an example of participatory citizenship activity for students?
questions.ex: Organising community clean-ups engages students in civic participation.

questions.q: Which river project supplies water to Sindh through canals?
options: Indus River irrigation system via Sukkur Barrage
questions.ex: Sukkur Barrage and associated canals distribute Indus water for Sindh irrigation.

questions.q: In Sindhi language, which word means 'friend'?
questions.ex: 'دوست' (dost) is used for friend in Sindhi, similar to Urdu.

questions.q: Which Urdu idiom means 'to waste time'?
options: ہاتھی کے دانت دکھانے کے اور
questions.ex: 'وقت کا ضیاع کرنا' literally means to waste time and is a common phrase.

questions.q: Which factor most influenced Sindh's cultural links with Arabia and Persia historically?
options: Geographical proximity via sea and trade routes
questions.ex: Maritime trade and proximity historically linked Sindh with Arabian and Persian cultures.

questions.q: When assessing student comprehension, which method gives the most diagnostic information?
questions.ex: Formative assessment provides ongoing, diagnostic insights into learning.

questions.q: Choose the correct Urdu antonym pair for 'آسان' (easy).
questions.ex: 'سخت' or 'مشکل' are antonyms for 'آسان'; 'مشکل' fits best as 'difficult'.

questions.q: Which landform is typical in upper Sindh around Sukkur?
options: Desert and rocky uplands with river terraces
questions.ex: Upper Sindh has desert areas and river terraces; alluvial plains are more central/lower Sindh.

questions.q: In Urdu sentence structure, which order is most common?
questions.ex: Urdu typically follows SOV word order: subject then object then verb.

questions.q: Which method helps teach plural formation to Urdu learners effectively?
options: Provide many examples and practice with nouns of different patterns
questions.ex: Showing patterns and varied practice helps learners internalize plural forms in Urdu.

questions.q: Which statement about citizenship rights is correct?
options: Rights have no limits and override others' rights
Rights may be balanced with public safety and laws
questions.ex: Rights are typically balanced against laws and public safety; they are not absolute.

questions.q: In Sindhi folk literature, Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is known for:
questions.ex: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai is celebrated for Sufi poetry central to Sindhi literature.

questions.q: Choose the correct Urdu translation for 'She will go to school later.'
options: وہ اسکول جائے گی بعد میں
وہ بعد میں اسکول جائے گی
